18/S0.subgoal: Recap the previous lecture's content and provide an overview of the tracking technologies to be discussed in the current lecture.

18/S1.subgoal: Describe the two types of electromechanical trackers: world-fixed and wearable.

18/S2.subgoal: Explain how electromagnetic trackers use magnetic fields and currents for position measurement.

18/S3.subgoal: Describe acoustic tracking and its similarities and differences with electromagnetic tracking.

18/S4.subgoal: Explain the categories of optical sensors used in vision-based tracking.

18/S5.subgoal: Describe infrared vision-based tracking, including outside-in and inside-out configurations.

18/S6.subgoal: Explain the three types of visible light-based tracking: fiducial, natural feature, and model-based.

18/S7.subgoal: Describe 3D structure tracking using depth sensors to create and track models.

18/S8.subgoal: Describe inertial trackers and the primary sensors used within them.

18/S9.subgoal: Explain GPS tracking and its application and limitations in different environments.

18/S10.subgoal: Describe motion capture systems and how they record human movements.

18/S11.subgoal: Explain eye-tracking systems and the techniques used to track gaze.

18/S12.subgoal: Explain hybrid tracking methods that combine multiple basic tracking technologies.

18/S13.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture and provide references.
